cards.text: Israel's long prayer to the LORD ends with a promise. In view of all of it, they'll make a binding agreement, put it in writing, and seal it with the names of their leaders, Levites and priests. Today, friend, the pens come out.

First name on the document is Nehemiah the governor, son of Hacaliah. Then the priests, the Levites and the leaders of the people sign, name after name after name. That's a longer list than the office birthday card, and NOBODY skipped it.

But the signers aren't the only ones in. The rest of the people step up too: priests, Levites, gatekeepers, singers, temple servants, and everyone who separated themselves from the people of the land to obey the Law of God.

cards.question: True or false: The wives of these people and their sons and daughters who are able to understand join in too.
All of these people join their noble brothers and make a sworn oath. What do they commit to?

answers.text: Follow the Law of God given through Moses
Rebuild the walls of every city in Judah
Send yearly gifts to the king of Persia

cards.text: They promise to carefully obey all of the LORD's commandments, ordinances and statutes. Then they get specific, and the first promise starts right at home with their families.

cards.question: First family promise: their daughters won't ___ the people of the land, and their sons won't either.

cards.text: Next up is the Sabbath. Say the people of the land show up with merchandise or grain to sell on the Sabbath day. A big shiny sale right on the holy day? Friend, I can feel the temptation from HERE.

cards.question: The people of the land are selling grain on the Sabbath. What does Israel promise?

answers.text: They won't buy from them that day
They'll buy only what they need
They'll trade goods instead of paying

cards.question: One more promise in that same breath. True or false: Every seventh year, Israel will let the fields lie fallow and cancel every debt.

cards.text: Now the oath turns to money. Israel puts itself under an obligation to give a third of a shekel every year.

cards.question: Israel promises a third of a shekel every year. What's that money for?

answers.text: The service of the house of God
Taxes for the king of Persia

cards.text: That money covers the showbread, the grain offerings and burnt offerings, the Sabbaths, the New Moons and feasts, and the sin offerings to make atonement for Israel. That is one HARD-working third of a shekel.

cards.question: Burning offerings on the altar takes fuel. So Israel casts lots among the priests, Levites and people. What are the lots for?

answers.text: Which families bring wood and when
Which men guard the city gates

cards.text: Year by year, they'll bring the firstfruits of their land and of every fruit tree to the house of the LORD. The FIRST, friend. Not the leftovers. Not the one that rolled under the counter.

cards.question: True or false: Israel will keep the firstborn of their herds and flocks at home.

cards.text: They'll also bring the priests the firstfruits of their grain offerings, their trees, their new wine and oil, AND their dough. DOUGH, friend! Now somebody's speaking my language.

cards.question: A tenth of Israel's produce belongs to the ___, and it's collected in all the towns where the people work.

cards.text: When the Levites go out to collect that tenth, they don't go alone. A priest of Aaron's line goes along with them.

cards.question: Then the Levites bring a ___ of those tithes to the ___ in the house of God.
The grain, new wine and oil all go to the storerooms where the priests, gatekeepers and singers stay. What's the big promise that wraps up Israel's oath?

answers.text: They won't neglect the house of their God
They'll build their God a bigger house

cards.text: And me? I'm STILL thinking about that dough. Stick around, friend, because this story isn't done.
